document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Secret] Open-source summary quoting a letter ostensibly signed by Jalaluddin Haqqani, whose network is 'very closely aligned with Al Qaeda', denouncing Mullah Omar. The letter is suspected to be a fake. ISAF analyst commentary calls separating the Taliban from al-Qaeda a farfetched concept, since the same low-level fighters are used by both and al-Qaeda plays a coordinating and strategic role.

events.description: Mullah Omar issued a statement seeking legitimate relations with all countries and expressing solidarity with Iran; Al Qaeda websites criticized the Taliban's nationalist trend.
First set of talks in Mecca between Afghan officials and former Taliban figures under the Saudi king's auspices.
Hekmatyar sent a second letter to Karzai, similar to the spring letter.
Coalition operation on a home in Kundi village, Khost, targeting a person affiliated with Al-Qa'ida; three killed, six detained per spokesman.
Kabul police shut down ERD Security Company and seized its weapons.

Mullah Omar issued a statement seeking legitimate relations with all countries and expressing solidarity with Iran; Al Qaeda websites then denounced the Taliban's nationalist, pro-Iranian orientation.
A letter signed with Jalaluddin Haqqani's name denounced Mullah Omar. Intelligence agents suspect the Afghan government or its allies forged it as a psychological operation.
The first set of talks between Afghan officials and former Taliban figures was held in Mecca under the auspices of the Saudi king.
Future meetings between Afghan officials and former Taliban figures were being planned in places like Dubai.
In the spring, Hekmatyar sent Karzai a letter implying that foreign troops should be removed from urban centers.
Hekmatyar sent Karzai a similar message in October.

Foreign forces raided a home in Kundi village; two men and a woman were killed, another woman was wounded, and three to six people were detained. The operation targeted an Al-Qa'ida-affiliated person.
Acting governor Sabari said foreign forces never inform Afghan authorities in advance of operations.
Hekmatyar sent a letter to Karzai saying he has dedicated his life to struggle but is old; another message followed in October.
Hekmatyar sent a similar message to Karzai.
Kabul police shut down ERD Security Company and seized its weapons (Kalashnikovs, 18 PK machine-guns, six pistols).
Foreign forces raided a home in Kundi village targeting an alleged Al-Qa'ida affiliate; two men and a woman killed, others wounded and detained (six per Sieber, three per locals).

key_claims: The CSM article reports Afghan government and allies are trying to split moderates from hard-liners and Al Qaeda from the Taliban.
Jalaluddin Haqqani heads an insurgent network independent of Mullah Omar's Taliban and very closely aligned with Al Qaeda.
A letter attributed to Haqqani denouncing Mullah Omar was suspected to be a government/ally psychological operation.
The ISAF analyst judges a Taliban-Al Qaeda split functionally unlikely, as the groups are not operationally fused and share low-level fighters.
Many Taliban financial resources reportedly come from Al Qaeda, and the Taliban have havens in Pakistan.
Hekmatyar's network is allied with the Taliban and he reportedly sought a senior government post.
